titulo: Accelerating the Radiology Learning Curve: How the Parameter-Based I-TIRADS Lexicon Enhances Interpretive Reliability and Learning Curves Across Resident Experience Levels—A Dynamic Video-Based Study

fig.label: Figure 2
fig.caption: Ultrasonographic spectrum of Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma (PTC) presenting with vertical orientation and metastatic lymphadenopathy: (a) Transverse ultrasound image of the right thyroid bed showing a 33(A) × 28(B) mm nodule (where A and B denote the maximum orthogonal caliper measurements) with a taller-than-wide orientation, patchy markedly hypoechoic areas, and ill-defined posterior margins—features that often contribute to interobserver variability (postoperative histopathological examination confirmed PTC); (b) Axial ultrasound image revealing a large, hypoechoic nodule with lobulated margins involving the right thyroid lobe (on the left) and a corresponding pathological lymph node at the right jugular chain level (on the right), characterized by a rounded shape and loss of the normal fatty hilum (postoperative histopathological evaluation confirmed metastatic involvement of the regional lymph node).
